clue.text: First offence on peninsula

parts.note: a crime is an offence against the law
A is the first letter and the mark of first rank, as in A1 or grade A

explanation.surface: Someone commits their first crime while holidaying on a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'First offence' as 'Crime A', the offence listed first, so the A follows CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a large peninsula jutting into the Black Sea.

clue.text: Brawl featuring vein of gold in season

indicators.note: the vein of gold sits inside the season, so 'in' signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, a season
a reef is a vein of ore, especially gold-bearing quartz in mining
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out over a gold seam discovered one autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly fight in which everyone joins, a general brawl.

clue.text: Notes on train crash from inner face of arch

indicators.note: in a down clue the notes are placed on, that is after, the crashed train
a train crash leaves the carriages jumbled, so the word train is rearranged

parts.note: do is the first note of the sol-fa scale, so dos are notes

explanation.surface: Musical notes written on a train crash report, from the inner face of an arch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' gives INTRA; in a down entry 'on' means placed after, a convention for down clues.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture the intrados is the inner curved surface, or soffit, of an arch.

clue.text: Playwright turned inside out by elements of former problem with Iceland

indicators.note: a letter from the inside of the phrase is turned out to its end, so one letter moves position

parts.words: elements of former problem with Iceland
parts.note: the Cod War was a past fishing dispute between Britain and Iceland, and its letters are the elements used

explanation.surface: A dramatist is radically reworked by the material of an old dispute with Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cod Wars were 1950s-70s fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland. 'turned inside out' moves the inner D of CODWAR out to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel Coward was an English dramatist, author of plays such as Private Lives and Blithe Spirit.

clue.text: Love among the brasses

indicators.note: the letter for love sits among the instruments, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: cornets are brass instruments
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms in the brass section of a band.
explanation.walkthrough: The light has no separate definition: it is the last word of the film Kind Hearts and Coronets, which several other clues cite as 21 25 and 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronets are small crowns worn by peers, completing the title of the Ealing film the puzzle celebrates.

clue.text: Uncertain farewell to opera?

parts.note: a wave is a gesture of farewell
the Ring is Wagner's cycle of operas, Der Ring des Nibelungen

explanation.surface: Is a goodbye at the opera house appropriate, someone wonders?
explanation.definitionFit: Wavering means hesitating between choices, so unsure or uncertain.

clue.text: Tell the world the leader's fled, being stricken

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of the is taken

parts.note: ran is a synonym of fled
smit is an old past participle of smite, meaning struck or stricken

explanation.surface: A broadcaster announces to everyone that the stricken leader has run away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'leader's' is a link meaning 'is'; SMIT is an archaic form, rarely met outside poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit is to broadcast a message, sending it out for everyone to receive.

clue.text: "21 25 are ___ 4 down" and Hamlet's uncle "… a little ___ most of 21 and less 8 21"

definitions.text: a little ___ most of 21 and less 8 21

explanation.surface: Two famous quotations, one Victorian and one Shakespearean, each with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson wrote 'Kind hearts are more than coronets'; Hamlet calls his uncle Claudius 'A little more than kin, and less than kind', and KIN is most of KIND.
explanation.definitionFit: Both quotations need the same comparative phrase in the gap, the one meaning exceeding or greater.

clue.text: See 7
Give a makeover to a parson in parliament?

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a parson
an MP is a Member of Parliament, someone sitting in parliament

explanation.surface: A clergyman elected to parliament is given a new image.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Rev. A., MP', a clergyman who is a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp something is to renovate or improve it, giving it a new look.

clue.text: Much panic with song "Growing globes"

indicators.note: much rather than all of the word is used, so its tail is dropped

parts.note: terror is a synonym of panic
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Much alarm greets a song titled Growing Globes.
explanation.definitionFit: Terraria are glass vessels, often spherical, in which plants are grown indoors.

clue.text: Opera gaining assent in which some blogs produce blue fluid

parts.note: Norma is Bellini's opera about a Druid priestess

indicators.note: a few letters of blogs go inside the word for assent, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a nod is a sign of assent

indicators.note: only some of the word blogs is used, so its tail is cut off

explanation.surface: An opera wins approval while some online writers produce a blue liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: Norma, not Aida or Tosca, is the opera here. 'blue fluid' is a jokey way of saying blue blood, aristocratic descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue blood is aristocratic descent, and Tennyson's Norman blood means the same noble ancestry.

clue.text: Dams bust during tease by such as Alexander or Macnamara

indicators.note: the broken dams sit within the teasing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: banter is teasing, playful joshing

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the letters of dams are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dams burst during some joking by men such as Alexander or Macnamara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' gives DMAS. Alexander's Ragtime Band (Irving Berlin) and Macnamara's Band (an Irish song) name their leaders, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander and Macnamara are the leaders in two well-known songs about bands, examples of band leaders.

clue.text: More evil from libellous person, to fake sickness with little change

indicators.note: only a small alteration is needed, one letter shifting place

parts.note: to malinger is to pretend illness to avoid work

explanation.surface: A slanderer feigns illness, hardly altering the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'libellous person' is a second definition: one who maligns. 'with little change' moves the N of MALINGER one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Malign means evil or harmful, and this is its comparative form, wickeder.

clue.text: Father to classical hero, not father to rights granted by companies to retail their products

indicators.note: not father means the abbreviation for father is removed

parts.words: rights granted by companies to retail their products
parts.note: franchises are licences to sell a company's goods
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A classical genealogy is muddled up with the language of retail licensing.
explanation.walkthrough: Anchises was the father of Aeneas, hero of Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend Anchises was the father of Aeneas, the Trojan hero of the Aeneid.

clue.text: Archbishop with school report of poet quoted here

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the poet's name is what is said aloud

parts.note: Tennyson wrote the lines this puzzle quotes, from Lady Clara Vere de Vere

explanation.surface: An archbishop's school report mentions the poet being quoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Archbishop Tenison's School in London is named after Thomas Tenison, Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tenison was Archbishop of Canterbury and founded the school that bears his name.

clue.text: I leave Japanese food, swallowing old coin, to apocryphal girl

indicators.note: the trimmed food takes the coin inside it, as if eating it
the letter I leaves, so it is removed from the food

parts.note: sushi is Japanese vinegared rice with fish
an anna was an old Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: I abandon my sushi, having swallowed an old coin, and complain to a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' leaves SUSH. The anna was an Indian coin, a staple of crosswords; Susanna appears in additions to the Book of Daniel.
explanation.definitionFit: Susannah is the heroine of the story of Susanna and the Elders in the Apocrypha.

clue.text: Don't have a place for rubbish outside the station

indicators.note: the bin goes outside, around the station's abbreviation

parts.note: a bin is where rubbish goes

explanation.surface: No dumping allowed: a rubbish bin stands outside the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't have' fits as in declining a drink: to abstain is to hold back from taking it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, choosing not to take something such as drink.

clue.text: "21 25 etc and ___ 8 11" — from Pisa (the film)

indicators.note: the answer is made out of these letters, rebuilt from them in a new order

explanation.surface: A famous quotation with a gap, apparently taken from a film set in Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'Kind hearts are more than coronets, and simple faith than Norman blood'; 'from' rebuilds PISA and THE FILM.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line sets plain trusting belief against noble descent; the gap holds that trusting belief.

clue.text: Salaried ruler on link road

parts.note: fee'd, given a fee, so paid or salaried
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A paid monarch sits on the road link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salaried' is read as FEE'D, given a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeder road carries traffic onto a main road, a connecting route.

clue.text: Stiffness not right for a prince?

indicators.note: not right means the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: rigor is stiffness, as in rigor mortis

explanation.surface: Being stiff and unbending is not right for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Igor is the title hero of Borodin's opera, a medieval Russian prince.

clue.text: Sort suit (see 7)

parts.note: kind is a synonym of sort
hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card player chooses a type of suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see 7' points to Tennyson's quotation in 7 down, whose opening words are the answer and the film's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's line opens with these words, which Ealing took for its 1949 comedy title.

clue.text: Little boy keeps most of 23 confused in 21 25 and 4 down

indicators.note: the boy's name holds the jumbled letters within it

parts.note: Gus is a short form of Augustus, a boy's name

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up, so they are rearranged
most rather than all of the word is used, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: the answer to 23 across, a first name

explanation.surface: A small boy keeps a garbled version of a name in the film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' leaves ENNIS, which 'confused' turns into INNES. The definition names the role: the actor who was in the film.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec Guinness famously played eight members of the D'Ascoyne family in the Ealing comedy.

clue.text: Price of 21 25 and 4 down was wrong returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: sinned means did wrong

explanation.surface: The cost of a film was misjudged, so it was sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price' looks like cost; it is the actor's surname. 'returned' turns SINNED round.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis Price played the murderous heir Louis Mazzini, so this is the given name of that actor.

clue.text: Embarrassed Spooner broke fast and went fast

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

parts.note: to break fast is to eat, so fed
raced means went fast

explanation.surface: An awkward moment: someone ate breakfast and then dashed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone embarrassed blushes, their face turning crimson with shame.
